label: read-track-3
in_my_words: Researchers are checking whether a simple rule about cell shape can predict why the hollow space inside little balls of dog kidney cells is dented instead of round. They are not doing new lab work. They use another team's published measurements and computer model, and they commit to their prediction before testing it.
how_in_my_words: They download the public data and keep a fingerprint of each file so it can't be swapped. They fit a trend line linking cell count to dentedness using normal cells only. Then they lock the settings in a dated file, like a sealed envelope. Next they score the locked model on other cell types it hasn't seen and compare it with dumb guesses (always round, the average, size only). They report the result either way, and they admit the test is only partly blind and that the photo days are mixed up with the cell types.

test_questions.question: What shape is the hollow often found to be, and what is it compared to?
test_questions.my_answer: Often dented, not round like a water balloon.

test_questions.question: What would show the researchers were wrong?
test_questions.my_answer: If the locked model is no better than the size-only line on normal cells held out by photo day, or can't beat always-round or the average.

test_questions.question: Why can't a cell-type difference be separated from a day difference?
test_questions.my_answer: Each cell type was photographed on different days.

test_questions.question: What actual result did the model get on the unseen cells?
test_questions.my_answer: The text doesn't say; only a leave-one-day-out check with numbers const 0.1396 and line 0.1214 is given, with no explanation of what it means.

test_questions.question: Who is right about pressure, the 2021 authors or the other lab?
test_questions.my_answer: Unknown. The text says it is still open.

sentences_i_could_not_follow: The best setting of the published model sweep looked worse than a plain average on normal cells, so the first check may fail.
Day-to-day spread in dentedness (about 0.07 on a 0-to-1 scale) is larger than some of the gaps we planned to detect.
One formula in the plan was written upside down and must be fixed first.
Two of the six planned tests lack enough data and may be dropped.
Our law library has no law about lumen shape, so no proof tool backs the biology.
what_would_help: Say up front what the one main prediction is, in a single sentence, and explain the "six planned tests", "published sweep" and "law library" before using them. Cut or explain the jargon in the check-yourself section, such as ANOVA, ICC and "const vs line".
